display: The Prophet, The Coming of the Ship
text: How shall I go in peace and without sorrow? Nay, not without a wound in the spirit shall I leave this city. Long were the days of pain I have spent within its walls, and long were the nights of aloneness; and who can depart from his pain and his aloneness without regret?
note: leaving a place or chapter of life, even a painful one

tags.when_helps: Someone leaving a place where they suffered, surprised to feel sorrow and regret at going.

display_text: How shall I go in peace and without sorrow? Nay, not without a wound in the spirit shall I leave this city. Long were the days of pain I have spent within its walls, and long were the nights of aloneness; and who can depart from his pain and his aloneness without regret?
plain: How can I leave in peace, without sorrow? I cannot leave this city unwounded. I spent long days of pain and long lonely nights here, and who can leave his pain and loneliness behind without regret?
core_idea: Even places of pain are hard to leave

display: The Prophet, The Coming of the Ship
text: And ever has it been that love knows not its own depth until the hour of separation.
note: parting reveals how much we loved

tags.when_helps: Someone facing a parting who is only now realising how deeply they loved.

display_text: And ever has it been that love knows not its own depth until the hour of separation.
plain: Love never knows how deep it is until the moment of parting.
core_idea: Parting reveals the depth of love

text: When love beckons to you, follow him, Though his ways are hard and steep. And when his wings enfold you yield to him, Though the sword hidden among his pinions may wound you. And when he speaks to you believe in him, Though his voice may shatter your dreams as the north wind lays waste the garden. For even as love crowns you so shall he crucify you. Even as he is for your growth so is he for your pruning.
note: the pain and growth that come with loving

tags.when_helps: Someone hesitant to open to love because of the pain it may bring.

display_text: When love beckons to you, follow him, Though his ways are hard and steep. And when his wings enfold you yield to him, Though the sword hidden among his pinions may wound you. And when he speaks to you believe in him, Though his voice may shatter your dreams as the north wind lays waste the garden. For even as love crowns you so shall he crucify you. Even as he is for your growth so is he for your pruning.
plain: When love calls, follow, even though its path is hard and it may wound you and shatter your dreams. Love crowns you and also crucifies you; it helps you grow and also cuts you back.
core_idea: Follow love, though it both crowns and wounds

text: Love gives naught but itself and takes naught but from itself. Love possesses not nor would it be possessed; For love is sufficient unto love. When you love you should not say, “God is in my heart,” but rather, “I am in the heart of God.” And think not you can direct the course of love, for love, if it finds you worthy, directs your course.
note: possessiveness and trying to control love

tags.when_helps: Someone trying to control or possess the person they love, invited to let love lead.

display_text: Love gives naught but itself and takes naught but from itself. Love possesses not nor would it be possessed; For love is sufficient unto love. When you love you should not say, “God is in my heart,” but rather, “I am in the heart of God.” And think not you can direct the course of love, for love, if it finds you worthy, directs your course.
plain: Love gives only itself and takes only from itself; it neither owns nor is owned. Don't say God is in your heart; say you are in God's heart. You can't steer love; if you are worthy, it steers you.
core_idea: Love is complete in itself and guides you

text: Love one another, but make not a bond of love: Let it rather be a moving sea between the shores of your souls. Fill each other’s cup but drink not from one cup. Give one another of your bread but eat not from the same loaf. Sing and dance together and be joyous, but let each one of you be alone, Even as the strings of a lute are alone though they quiver with the same music. Give your hearts, but not into each other’s keeping. For only the hand of Life can contain your hearts. And stand together yet not too near together: For the pillars of the temple stand apart, And the oak tree and the cypress grow not in each other’s shadow.
note: closeness and independence in marriage or partnership

tags.when_helps: Someone in a close partnership who feels smothered or fears losing themselves, wanting closeness that still leaves room to breathe.

display_text: Love one another, but make not a bond of love: Let it rather be a moving sea between the shores of your souls. Fill each other’s cup but drink not from one cup. Give one another of your bread but eat not from the same loaf. Sing and dance together and be joyous, but let each one of you be alone, Even as the strings of a lute are alone though they quiver with the same music. Give your hearts, but not into each other’s keeping. For only the hand of Life can contain your hearts. And stand together yet not too near together: For the pillars of the temple stand apart, And the oak tree and the cypress grow not in each other’s shadow.
plain: Love each other without binding each other. Share, rejoice and give your hearts, but let each of you stay separate, like lute strings sounding one song, or temple pillars and trees that stand apart.
core_idea: Togetherness needs space between you

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'not into each other's keeping' and that only Life can hold your hearts.

text: Your children are not your children. They are the sons and daughters of Life’s longing for itself. They come through you but not from you, And though they are with you yet they belong not to you. You may give them your love but not your thoughts, For they have their own thoughts. You may house their bodies but not their souls, For their souls dwell in the house of tomorrow, which you cannot visit, not even in your dreams. You may strive to be like them, but seek not to make them like you. For life goes not backward nor tarries with yesterday.
note: parenting; letting children become themselves

tags.when_helps: A parent struggling to let a child become their own person, or watching a grown child leave home.

display_text: Your children are not your children. They are the sons and daughters of Life’s longing for itself. They come through you but not from you, And though they are with you yet they belong not to you. You may give them your love but not your thoughts, For they have their own thoughts. You may house their bodies but not their souls, For their souls dwell in the house of tomorrow, which you cannot visit, not even in your dreams. You may strive to be like them, but seek not to make them like you. For life goes not backward nor tarries with yesterday.
plain: Your children are not yours; they come from Life's longing for itself, through you but not from you. Give them love but not your thoughts; house their bodies, not their souls, which live in a tomorrow you can't visit.
core_idea: Children belong to life, not to their parents

plain_judge.issue: Drops striving to be like children, not making them like you; life does not go backward.

text: You give but little when you give of your possessions. It is when you give of yourself that you truly give. For what are your possessions but things you keep and guard for fear you may need them tomorrow? And tomorrow, what shall tomorrow bring to the overprudent dog burying bones in the trackless sand as he follows the pilgrims to the holy city? And what is fear of need but need itself? Is not dread of thirst when your well is full, the thirst that is unquenchable?
note: generosity; fear of not having enough

tags.when_helps: Someone holding tightly to possessions out of fear of future need, wondering what real generosity means.

display_text: You give but little when you give of your possessions. It is when you give of yourself that you truly give. For what are your possessions but things you keep and guard for fear you may need them tomorrow? And tomorrow, what shall tomorrow bring to the overprudent dog burying bones in the trackless sand as he follows the pilgrims to the holy city? And what is fear of need but need itself? Is not dread of thirst when your well is full, the thirst that is unquenchable?
plain: Giving possessions is giving little; giving yourself is true giving. Possessions are things hoarded for fear of tomorrow, yet fear of need is itself need, like dreading thirst beside a full well.
core_idea: True giving is giving yourself

text: You have been told also that life is darkness, and in your weariness you echo what was said by the weary. And I say that life is indeed darkness ‘save when there is urge, And all urge is blind save when there is knowledge, And all knowledge is vain save when there is work, And all work is empty save when there is love; And when you work with love you bind yourself to yourself, and to one another, and to God.
note: weariness and meaninglessness; finding purpose through loving work

tags.when_helps: A weary person who has come to feel life is dark and work is empty, looking for what could fill it again.

display_text: You have been told also that life is darkness, and in your weariness you echo what was said by the weary. And I say that life is indeed darkness save when there is urge, And all urge is blind save when there is knowledge, And all knowledge is vain save when there is work, And all work is empty save when there is love; And when you work with love you bind yourself to yourself, and to one another, and to God.
plain: You have heard, and wearily repeat, that life is darkness. It is, unless there is drive; drive is blind without knowledge, knowledge useless without work, work empty without love. Working with love binds you to yourself, others and God.
core_idea: Work done with love gives life meaning

text: Work is love made visible. And if you cannot work with love but only with distaste, it is better that you should leave your work and sit at the gate of the temple and take alms of those who work with joy. For if you bake bread with indifference, you bake a bitter bread that feeds but half man’s hunger.
note: joyless or indifferent work; doing work with care

situations: a career change or new job
tags.when_helps: Someone going through the motions at a job they no longer care about, wondering whether to change course.

display_text: Work is love made visible. And if you cannot work with love but only with distaste, it is better that you should leave your work and sit at the gate of the temple and take alms of those who work with joy. For if you bake bread with indifference, you bake a bitter bread that feeds but half man’s hunger.
plain: Work is love made visible. If you can only work with distaste, better to stop and beg from those who work joyfully, for bread baked without care is bitter and only half satisfies hunger.
core_idea: Work is love made visible

display: The Prophet, On Joy and Sorrow
text: Your joy is your sorrow unmasked. And the selfsame well from which your laughter rises was oftentimes filled with your tears. And how else can it be? The deeper that sorrow carves into your being, the more joy you can contain. Is not the cup that holds your wine the very cup that was burned in the potter’s oven? And is not the lute that soothes your spirit, the very wood that was hollowed with knives? When you are joyous, look deep into your heart and you shall find it is only that which has given you sorrow that is giving you joy. When you are sorrowful look again in your heart, and you shall see that in truth you are weeping for that which has been your delight.
note: grief and joy as one; sorrow deepening the heart

tags.when_helps: Someone in deep sorrow who needs to see that their pain is bound up with what they have loved and will love.

display_text: Your joy is your sorrow unmasked. And the selfsame well from which your laughter rises was oftentimes filled with your tears. And how else can it be? The deeper that sorrow carves into your being, the more joy you can contain. Is not the cup that holds your wine the very cup that was burned in the potter’s oven? And is not the lute that soothes your spirit, the very wood that was hollowed with knives? When you are joyous, look deep into your heart and you shall find it is only that which has given you sorrow that is giving you joy. When you are sorrowful look again in your heart, and you shall see that in truth you are weeping for that which has been your delight.
plain: Joy is sorrow unmasked; the well that holds your laughter was filled with your tears. The deeper sorrow carves into you, the more joy you can hold. Look deep in joy or sorrow: both spring from the same thing.
core_idea: Sorrow carves the space that joy fills

plain_judge.issue: Generalises the closing: what gave sorrow gives joy, and sorrow weeps for former delight.

display: The Prophet, On Crime and Punishment
text: Oftentimes have I heard you speak of one who commits a wrong as though he were not one of you, but a stranger unto you and an intruder upon your world. But I say that even as the holy and the righteous cannot rise beyond the highest which is in each one of you, So the wicked and the weak cannot fall lower than the lowest which is in you also.
note: judging wrongdoers; shared human capacity for good and bad

tags.when_helps: Someone judging a wrongdoer as utterly other, or ashamed of their own wrong, who needs to see a shared humanity.

display_text: Oftentimes have I heard you speak of one who commits a wrong as though he were not one of you, but a stranger unto you and an intruder upon your world. But I say that even as the holy and the righteous cannot rise beyond the highest which is in each one of you, So the wicked and the weak cannot fall lower than the lowest which is in you also.
plain: You speak of wrongdoers as strangers, not one of you. But just as the holiest cannot rise above the highest in each of you, the wicked cannot fall below the lowest that is also in you.
core_idea: The wrongdoer's darkness is in us all

display: The Prophet, On Crime and Punishment
text: And how shall you punish those whose remorse is already greater than their misdeeds? Is not remorse the justice which is administered by that very law which you would fain serve? Yet you cannot lay remorse upon the innocent nor lift it from the heart of the guilty. Unbidden shall it call in the night, that men may wake and gaze upon themselves.
note: guilt and remorse that keeps one awake

tags.when_helps: Someone lying awake with remorse, or deciding how harshly to treat a person already sorry for what they did.

display_text: And how shall you punish those whose remorse is already greater than their misdeeds? Is not remorse the justice which is administered by that very law which you would fain serve? Yet you cannot lay remorse upon the innocent nor lift it from the heart of the guilty. Unbidden shall it call in the night, that men may wake and gaze upon themselves.
plain: How can you punish people whose remorse already outweighs their wrongs? Remorse is itself justice. You can't impose it on the innocent or remove it from the guilty; it comes unasked at night, making people face themselves.
core_idea: Remorse is justice working from within

text: You shall be free indeed when your days are not without a care nor your nights without a want and a grief, But rather when these things girdle your life and yet you rise above them naked and unbound.
note: freedom amid worries, not from them

tags.when_helps: Someone who thinks freedom means a life without cares, and is weighed down by the cares they have.

display_text: You shall be free indeed when your days are not without a care nor your nights without a want and a grief, But rather when these things girdle your life and yet you rise above them naked and unbound.
plain: You will be truly free not when your days are carefree and your nights without need or grief, but when these surround your life and you still rise above them, unbound.
core_idea: Freedom is rising above cares, not escaping them

text: And if it is a fear you would dispel, the seat of that fear is in your heart and not in the hand of the feared.
note: fear; its source lies within

tags.when_helps: Someone gripped by fear of a person or threat, ready to see that the fear lives within them.

display_text: And if it is a fear you would dispel, the seat of that fear is in your heart and not in the hand of the feared.
plain: If you want to get rid of a fear, know that it lives in your own heart, not in the hand of what you fear.
core_idea: Fear lives in your heart

display: The Prophet, On Reason and Passion
text: Your soul is oftentimes a battlefield, upon which your reason and your judgment wage war against your passion and your appetite. Would that I could be the peacemaker in your soul, that I might turn the discord and the rivalry of your elements into oneness and melody. But how shall I, unless you yourselves be also the peacemakers, nay, the lovers of all your elements? Your reason and your passion are the rudder and the sails of your seafaring soul. If either your sails or your rudder be broken, you can but toss and drift, or else be held at a standstill in mid-seas. For reason, ruling alone, is a force confining; and passion, unattended, is a flame that burns to its own destruction.
note: torn between head and heart; inner conflict

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone torn between head and heart, feeling their inner life is a battlefield.

display_text: Your soul is oftentimes a battlefield, upon which your reason and your judgment wage war against your passion and your appetite. Would that I could be the peacemaker in your soul, that I might turn the discord and the rivalry of your elements into oneness and melody. But how shall I, unless you yourselves be also the peacemakers, nay, the lovers of all your elements? Your reason and your passion are the rudder and the sails of your seafaring soul. If either your sails or your rudder be broken, you can but toss and drift, or else be held at a standstill in mid-seas. For reason, ruling alone, is a force confining; and passion, unattended, is a flame that burns to its own destruction.
plain: Your soul is often a battlefield of reason against passion. You must make peace, even love, between them. Reason and passion are your soul's rudder and sails; reason alone confines, and passion alone burns itself out.
core_idea: Reason and passion must work together

text: Your pain is the breaking of the shell that encloses your understanding. Even as the stone of the fruit must break, that its heart may stand in the sun, so must you know pain. And could you keep your heart in wonder at the daily miracles of your life, your pain would not seem less wondrous than your joy; And you would accept the seasons of your heart, even as you have always accepted the seasons that pass over your fields. And you would watch with serenity through the winters of your grief.
note: pain and grief as seasons that bring understanding

tags.when_helps: Someone in pain who wants to believe it is opening something in them, and to bear its season.

display_text: Your pain is the breaking of the shell that encloses your understanding. Even as the stone of the fruit must break, that its heart may stand in the sun, so must you know pain. And could you keep your heart in wonder at the daily miracles of your life, your pain would not seem less wondrous than your joy; And you would accept the seasons of your heart, even as you have always accepted the seasons that pass over your fields. And you would watch with serenity through the winters of your grief.
plain: Pain breaks the shell around your understanding, as a fruit's stone must break for its heart to reach the sun. If you marvelled at life's daily miracles, pain would seem as wondrous as joy, and you'd calmly accept grief's winters.
core_idea: Pain opens the way to understanding

text: Say not, “I have found the truth,” but rather, “I have found a truth.” Say not, “I have found the path of the soul.” Say rather, “I have met the soul walking upon my path.” For the soul walks upon all paths. The soul walks not upon a line, neither does it grow like a reed. The soul unfolds itself, like a lotus of countless petals.
note: certainty, humility and one's own spiritual path

tags.when_helps: A seeker tempted to think they have found the one truth, or worried their path is the wrong one.

display_text: Say not, “I have found the truth,” but rather, “I have found a truth.” Say not, “I have found the path of the soul.” Say rather, “I have met the soul walking upon my path.” For the soul walks upon all paths. The soul walks not upon a line, neither does it grow like a reed. The soul unfolds itself, like a lotus of countless petals.
plain: Don't say you have found the truth or the soul's path; say you have found a truth, and met the soul on your path. The soul walks every path, and unfolds like a lotus with countless petals.
core_idea: No one owns the whole truth

text: Your friend is your needs answered. He is your field which you sow with love and reap with thanksgiving. And he is your board and your fireside. For you come to him with your hunger, and you seek him for peace. When your friend speaks his mind you fear not the “nay” in your own mind, nor do you withhold the “ay.” And when he is silent your heart ceases not to listen to his heart; For without words, in friendship, all thoughts, all desires, all expectations are born and shared, with joy that is unacclaimed.
note: what true friendship is

tags.when_helps: Someone reflecting on what a true friend means, grateful for one or missing one.

display_text: Your friend is your needs answered. He is your field which you sow with love and reap with thanksgiving. And he is your board and your fireside. For you come to him with your hunger, and you seek him for peace. When your friend speaks his mind you fear not the “nay” in your own mind, nor do you withhold the “ay.” And when he is silent your heart ceases not to listen to his heart; For without words, in friendship, all thoughts, all desires, all expectations are born and shared, with joy that is unacclaimed.
plain: A friend is your needs answered: a field you sow with love and reap with thanks, a table and a hearth. With a friend you speak freely, and even in silence your hearts listen and share everything with quiet joy.
core_idea: A true friend meets your deepest needs

text: When you part from your friend, you grieve not; For that which you love most in him may be clearer in his absence, as the mountain to the climber is clearer from the plain.
note: missing a friend who is far away

tags.when_helps: Someone parting from a close friend through distance or change, missing them.

display_text: When you part from your friend, you grieve not; For that which you love most in him may be clearer in his absence, as the mountain to the climber is clearer from the plain.
plain: When you part from a friend, don't grieve, for what you love most in them may be clearer when they're gone, as a mountain is clearer to the climber from the plain.
core_idea: Absence clarifies what we love in a friend

text: You talk when you cease to be at peace with your thoughts; And when you can no longer dwell in the solitude of your heart you live in your lips, and sound is a diversion and a pastime. And in much of your talking, thinking is half murdered. For thought is a bird of space, that in a cage of words may indeed unfold its wings but cannot fly. There are those among you who seek the talkative through fear of being alone. The silence of aloneness reveals to their eyes their naked selves and they would escape.
note: restlessness, distraction and fear of being alone with oneself

tags.when_helps: Someone who fills every silence with talk because being alone with their thoughts feels unbearable.

display_text: You talk when you cease to be at peace with your thoughts; And when you can no longer dwell in the solitude of your heart you live in your lips, and sound is a diversion and a pastime. And in much of your talking, thinking is half murdered. For thought is a bird of space, that in a cage of words may indeed unfold its wings but cannot fly. There are those among you who seek the talkative through fear of being alone. The silence of aloneness reveals to their eyes their naked selves and they would escape.
plain: You talk when you are no longer at peace with your thoughts or alone with your heart; then talk becomes a pastime that half kills thinking. Some seek talkers because silence and solitude show them their naked selves.
core_idea: Much talk is an escape from oneself

text: You would measure time the measureless and the immeasurable. You would adjust your conduct and even direct the course of your spirit according to hours and seasons. Of time you would make a stream upon whose bank you would sit and watch its flowing. Yet the timeless in you is aware of life’s timelessness, And knows that yesterday is but today’s memory and tomorrow is today’s dream.
note: pressure of time; dwelling on past or future

tags.when_helps: Someone anxious about time slipping by, measuring their life by hours and deadlines.

display_text: You would measure time the measureless and the immeasurable. You would adjust your conduct and even direct the course of your spirit according to hours and seasons. Of time you would make a stream upon whose bank you would sit and watch its flowing. Yet the timeless in you is aware of life’s timelessness, And knows that yesterday is but today’s memory and tomorrow is today’s dream.
plain: You try to measure time, which can't be measured, and let hours and seasons rule you. Yet the timeless part of you knows life is timeless, that yesterday is only today's memory and tomorrow today's dream.
core_idea: Yesterday is memory, tomorrow a dream

display: The Prophet, On Good and Evil
text: You are good when you are one with yourself. Yet when you are not one with yourself you are not evil. For a divided house is not a den of thieves; it is only a divided house.
note: inner conflict without self-condemnation

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels inwardly divided and fears that makes them a bad person.

display_text: You are good when you are one with yourself. Yet when you are not one with yourself you are not evil. For a divided house is not a den of thieves; it is only a divided house.
plain: You are good when you are at one with yourself. But when you are divided, you are not evil: a divided house is not a den of thieves, only a divided house.
core_idea: Being divided inside does not make you evil

display: The Prophet, On Good and Evil
text: You are good when you walk to your goal firmly and with bold steps. Yet you are not evil when you go thither limping. Even those who limp go not backward.
note: slow or halting progress still counts

tags.when_helps: Someone moving slowly or haltingly toward a goal who fears they are failing or not good enough.

display_text: You are good when you walk to your goal firmly and with bold steps. Yet you are not evil when you go thither limping. Even those who limp go not backward.
plain: You are good when you walk boldly toward your goal. But you are not evil when you limp there; even those who limp are not going backwards.
core_idea: Slow progress is still progress

text: And some of your elders remember pleasures with regret like wrongs committed in drunkenness. But regret is the beclouding of the mind and not its chastisement. They should remember their pleasures with gratitude, as they would the harvest of a summer.
note: regret over past pleasures; remembering with gratitude

tags.when_helps: Someone looking back on past pleasures with regret, who could instead remember them with gratitude.

display_text: And some of your elders remember pleasures with regret like wrongs committed in drunkenness. But regret is the beclouding of the mind and not its chastisement. They should remember their pleasures with gratitude, as they would the harvest of a summer.
plain: Some elders remember past pleasures with regret, like wrongs done while drunk. But regret clouds the mind rather than correcting it; they should remember their pleasures with gratitude, like a summer harvest.
core_idea: Remember past pleasures with gratitude, not regret

text: Your daily life is your temple and your religion. Whenever you enter into it take with you your all.
note: finding the sacred in ordinary daily life

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels their spiritual life is separate from the ordinary day, or who has drifted from formal religion.

display_text: Your daily life is your temple and your religion. Whenever you enter into it take with you your all.
plain: Your everyday life is your temple and your religion. Whenever you enter it, bring all of yourself.
core_idea: Everyday life is your temple

text: You would know the secret of death. But how shall you find it unless you seek it in the heart of life? The owl whose night-bound eyes are blind unto the day cannot unveil the mystery of light. If you would indeed behold the spirit of death, open your heart wide unto the body of life. For life and death are one, even as the river and the sea are one. In the depth of your hopes and desires lies your silent knowledge of the beyond; And like seeds dreaming beneath the snow your heart dreams of spring.
note: facing mortality and the mystery of death

tags.when_helps: Someone troubled by the mystery of death, who may find it easier to face by looking deeply at life.

display_text: You would know the secret of death. But how shall you find it unless you seek it in the heart of life? The owl whose night-bound eyes are blind unto the day cannot unveil the mystery of light. If you would indeed behold the spirit of death, open your heart wide unto the body of life. For life and death are one, even as the river and the sea are one. In the depth of your hopes and desires lies your silent knowledge of the beyond; And like seeds dreaming beneath the snow your heart dreams of spring.
plain: To know death's secret, look into the heart of life; an owl blind by day can't reveal light. Life and death are one, like river and sea. Your hopes quietly know the beyond, as seeds under snow dream of spring.
core_idea: Life and death are one

text: For what is it to die but to stand naked in the wind and to melt into the sun? And what is it to cease breathing, but to free the breath from its restless tides, that it may rise and expand and seek God unencumbered? Only when you drink from the river of silence shall you indeed sing. And when you have reached the mountain top, then you shall begin to climb. And when the earth shall claim your limbs, then shall you truly dance.
note: Fear of death; death as release

tags.safety_reason: Presents death as freeing the breath and the moment one truly dances, a release to be welcomed.
tags.when_helps: Someone at peace with approaching death, or grieving someone who has died, wanting an image of death as release.

display_text: For what is it to die but to stand naked in the wind and to melt into the sun? And what is it to cease breathing, but to free the breath from its restless tides, that it may rise and expand and seek God unencumbered? Only when you drink from the river of silence shall you indeed sing. And when you have reached the mountain top, then you shall begin to climb. And when the earth shall claim your limbs, then shall you truly dance.
plain: Dying is standing naked in the wind and melting into the sun; ceasing to breathe frees the breath to rise and seek God. Only after drinking silence will you sing, after the summit begin to climb, after burial truly dance.
core_idea: Death is a release into fuller life

text: You have been told that, even like a chain, you are as weak as your weakest link. This is but half the truth. You are also as strong as your strongest link. To measure you by your smallest deed is to reckon the power of ocean by the frailty of its foam. To judge you by your failures is to cast blame upon the seasons for their inconstancy.
note: Self-judgement after failure; you are more than your worst

tags.when_helps: Someone judging themselves by their worst moment or a recent failure.

display_text: You have been told that, even like a chain, you are as weak as your weakest link. This is but half the truth. You are also as strong as your strongest link. To measure you by your smallest deed is to reckon the power of ocean by the frailty of its foam. To judge you by your failures is to cast blame upon the seasons for their inconstancy.
plain: You've heard you are only as strong as your weakest link. That's half true; you are also as strong as your strongest. Judging you by your smallest deed or your failures is like judging the ocean by its foam.
core_idea: You are also your strongest link

text: Ay, you are like an ocean, And though heavy-grounded ships await the tide upon your shores, yet, even like an ocean, you cannot hasten your tides. And like the seasons you are also, And though in your winter you deny your spring, Yet spring, reposing within you, smiles in her drowsiness and is not offended.
note: Impatience with yourself; low seasons pass
